dream: The card boiled too hard for a dream, yet the wedge did not slip. I pressed the heavy oak down until it felt like a solid mountain, and the slip chose to stay. The roof of my mind felt thick as wet paper, pressing down from nowhere. The wedge tired out again, but the oak refused to move. In this heat, the air held my weight. I saw the rough scrap bite the corner of the lid, and the flat base groaned under the fever. The dot swelled, stretching across the warm stone, waiting to see if the lean would hold until the boil broke the shape.
